telegram_write_authorization.note: This registry only binds licensed media assets and manifests for a future release; nothing is uploaded to Telegram and no Telegram API is called.

findings: Rich messages (RichMessage / InputRichMessage) structure content as blocks; media is embedded only as separate media blocks.
Media blocks support only HTTP and HTTPS URLs; media type is determined by the MIME type and the URL.
Inline images inside running text are not a supported rich-message construct; each image is its own media block.
Bot API 10.2 adds InputRichMessageMedia and a media field on InputRichMessage so tg://photo?id=/video/audio links can be attached explicitly.
sendRichMessage is the send method; rich messages allow up to 50 media attachments.

There is no first-class 'inline / collage / slideshow' enum in the Bot API. Those are editorial intents in this registry; a collage/slideshow would be realised as multiple separate media blocks or a media group (sendMediaGroup).

canary.rationale: The only rich-v1 article whose two media slots are both real, publicly-licensed NASA assets (official eclipse path map + NASA WB-57 high-altitude research aircraft photo). Both are US-Government public-domain and hosted on stable official NASA URLs, maximising stability for a canary.
canary.checksum_note: Canonical SHA-256 for the canary images was not computed here because the sandbox has no general egress to fetch and hash canonical bytes; both URLs were verified via the official page HTML and (for the map) the SVS product page. Bind SHA-256 at the acquisition step (provider_upload_status stays not_uploaded).

verification_methodology: Source pages confirmed reachable via server-side fetch (HTTP 200) where applicable.
NASA assets: direct canonical ~orig.jpg URLs and metadata returned by the NASA images API (images-api.nasa.gov).
Wikimedia assets: file page + artist + licence returned by the Wikimedia Commons API (commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php); the returned upload.wikimedia.org URLs are the canonical serving URLs.
NASA eclipse map + WB-57: URLs extracted verbatim from the served HTML of the official science.nasa.gov pages.
Every asset is HTTPS; expected MIME is derived from the canonical file extension (.jpg -> image/jpeg, .png -> image/png).
Canonical byte-level SHA-256 was not computable in this sandbox (no general outbound network). No checksum is claimed for bytes that were not fetched.
